key_decisions.decision: Clock domain for timers and watchdog
key_decisions.ma_choice: Single PCLK domain; WDT ticks from a PCLK prescaler; no CDC inside the block
key_decisions.plan_choice: D1: single PCLK domain, WDT counts on PRESC-generated PCLK ticks
key_decisions.note: The spec lists only PCLK and defines WDT PRESC in PCLK cycles.

key_decisions.ma_choice: apb_regif decoder/mux, two generate-instanced tmr_core, one wdt_core with the lock inside it, IRQ status/enable regs inline at top
key_decisions.plan_choice: APB decoder, 2 timer instances, WDT core, separate lock unit, output logic
key_decisions.note: Placing the lock flop as a separate unit rather than inside wdt_core is a cosmetic difference.

key_decisions.decision: PSLVERR scope and handling of illegal accesses to mapped registers
key_decisions.ma_choice: PSLVERR = acc & ~mapped only; writes to RO or locked registers are silently ignored; WDT_KICK reads 0
key_decisions.plan_choice: D2: PSLVERR only for unmapped offsets; RO and locked writes ignored; KICK reads 0

key_decisions.ma_choice: Decode PADDR[11:2] only and ignore the low bits

key_decisions.decision: Same-cycle collision priorities (RW1C vs hardware set, CTRL write vs one-shot EN clear, LOAD write vs tick)
key_decisions.ma_choice: Hardware set wins over W1C; software CTRL write wins over the one-shot EN clear; a LOAD write wins over a tick and suppresses that tick's events
key_decisions.plan_choice: D4: hardware set wins, software CTRL write wins; LOAD-vs-tick is listed as a corner case to resolve
key_decisions.note: The plan does not explicitly state that a LOAD-write tick suppresses its events, but the main priority rules agree.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Tick when pcnt >= presc, so lowering PRESC mid-count is safe; the prescaler is held at 0 while EN=0 and cleared on a LOAD write
key_decisions.note: The plan only says this behaviour 'is stated' in S4 done_when, without making a choice.

key_decisions.ma_choice: A periodic reload to a value equal to CMP fires CMP; a LOAD write equal to CMP does not
key_decisions.plan_choice: S4: a reload equal to CMP sets CMP (tick-caused); a LOAD write does not

key_decisions.decision: CMP suppression on the one-shot expiry tick
key_decisions.ma_choice: cmp_evt is masked on the one-shot expiry tick, so CMP=0 fires only once
key_decisions.note: The plan does not address the double-fire hazard when CMP=0 in one-shot mode.

key_decisions.ma_choice: timer_irq = |(status & en) and wdt_irq = warn & int_en, both combinational from flops; wdt_rst_req is registered
key_decisions.plan_choice: D5: combinational AND/OR from flops; sticky rst_req flop

key_decisions.decision: Effect of a WDT_LOAD write or EN set on WDT_VALUE
key_decisions.ma_choice: No reload; only kick_ok, wexpire or a tick change wvalue
Sets WIN_VIOL and rst_req if RES_EN; no reload and no WARN clear
Reload and keep counting with WARN still set
key_decisions.plan_choice: D8: reload and keep counting, WARN stays set

key_decisions.ma_choice: wtick is gated by ~rst_req_q, so the counter freezes until PRESETn
key_decisions.note: The plan only ensures rst_req is sticky; counter behaviour in the FIRED state is not decided.

key_decisions.decision: WARN next-state priority and a kick while disabled
key_decisions.ma_choice: kick_ok clears > first expiry sets > W1C clear; a kick while EN=0 still reloads and clears WARN
key_decisions.note: The plan lists the kick-vs-expiry and kick-while-disabled cases as to-be-stated but gives no resolution. Only hardware set over W1C is decided.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Async assert, sync de-assert (at SoC level), active-low PRESETn
key_decisions.plan_choice: D12: async active-low; system synchronises deassertion

summary: The plan is well aligned with the MA on all major visible-behaviour choices: single clock, partition, PSLVERR scope, collision priorities, combinational IRQs, WDT_LOAD/EN not reloading, window-violation semantics, RES_EN=0 re-expiry and the wrong-key policy. Both questions asked addressed real spec gaps. The gaps are several lower-level control decisions the MA makes explicitly and the plan defers without choosing: the >= prescaler compare and prescaler reset on EN=0, CMP suppression on the one-shot expiry tick, freezing the WDT counter after rst_req, and the full WARN priority ordering including a kick while disabled. The plan also adds a WDT prescaler restart on kick, which the MA does not describe.
